newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-TAKE YOUR CHOICE FROM TURKEY'S BIG FOUR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TAKE YOUR CHOICE FROM TURKEY'S BIG FOUR.

text.p: Few people predict the Turkish league kicking off this weekend will be anything other than a four-horse race.

Between them Istanbul teams Besiktas, Fenerbahce and Galatasaray plus Trabzonspor from the Black Sea have taken every title since the league began in 1959 and it is the matches between them which really decide the honours.
Defending champions Galatasaray look the strongest of the Big Four again this year.
"We have built a team here. I have a squad to take three cups this season. I have faith in my players," said Galatasaray coach Fatih Terim, who is going into his second year at the club.
Terim's team is directed from midfield by Romanian Gheorghe Hagi, while forward Hakan Sukur -- with 38 goals last season -- provides the strike force.
Hagi's fellow countrymen Iulian Filipescu, Adrian Ilie and new signing from Barcelona Gheorghe Popescu give the squad added depth.
Cross-town rivals Besiktas and Fenerbahce have to adapt to new systems under new foreign coaches not yet used to the microscopic scrutiny and wild expectations of this soccer-obsessed nation.
Besiktas, under new boss Welshman John Toshack, have been beset with injuries and disasters during the close season and have a big hole in midfield after the departure of Yalcin.

But the return to fitness of Nigerian striker Daniel Amokachi and the signing of one of the stars of Bulgaria's 1994 World Cup campaign, Yordan Lechkov, should strengthen the side ahead of European Cup matches next month.
"We have to turn our disadvantages into advantages in a very short time by working very hard," Toshack said.

Fenerbahce, with their third trainer in less than a year, had a similarly disappointing run-up to the season. New Yugoslav coach Otto Baric was not pleased with his team's performance and listed the failings of his players one by one.

"Bolic is not at the required level, Ilie (Adrian's brother, Sabin) has not been able to fit into the team. Saffet is off form. Okocha, Tarik, Ibrahim and Ilker are making passing mistakes and Uche and Hogh haven't got used to the new system," he said.
Trabzonspor, fourth last year, have not won the league since 1981 but are still seen as a serious threat.
"My players have an extraordinary desire to win the championship this season," said trainer Yilmaz Vural.

Trabzonspor sold Georgian brothers Sota and Arcil Arveladze and compatriot George Nemsadze during the close season, replacing them with the untried combination of Czech Karel Rada, Croatian Davor Vugrinec and Cameroon's Jean-Jacques Misse-Misse.
Outside the big four, the lesser teams acknowledge the limit of their ambitions.
"Our aim is fifth place," admitted Istanbulspor coach Saffet Susic.
Despite heavy investment -- they paid a Turkish record $7.9 million for playmaker Sergen Yalcin -- Istanbulspor and other fifth-placed contenders can hope for little more.
